article.body_html:
Three rules can sit behind the single word "fuel" on a rental agreement: bring the bike back with the same amount you started with, bring it back full, or pay for the fuel you used. Each is workable. The trouble starts when the two sides of the counter think they agreed different ones, and nobody wrote down the level the bike left with. This guide is about settling the rule and the starting level at pickup, when everyone is calm, so that return day holds no argument.

The three rules, and what each asks of you

RuleWhat you do at returnWhat you must record at pickup
Same level as at pickupTop up until the gauge shows what it showed when you leftA photo of the gauge, taken in daylight, with the odometer in the same frame
Full on returnFill the tank before you reach the shopWhether the tank was full when you took the bike, because a bike that left half empty makes this rule unfair
Pay for fuel usedReturn the bike as it is and settle the differenceThe starting level, the odometer, and how the fuel is priced

This guide does not say which rule Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà uses, because that is for the shop to say. Ask it: "On return, should the bike come back with the same level, full, or do you charge for the fuel used?" Write down the answer, the date and who gave it.

Record the starting level properly

  1. Read the gauge with the ignition on (do not start the bike) and the bike on level ground; if the shop offers to put it on the centre stand, let it, and do not lift it yourself.
  2. Photograph the gauge and the odometer together, close enough to read, and keep the original file, which stores the date and time.
  3. Ask the shop what the level was meant to be. A digital gauge showing three of four bars, or a needle between two marks, is easy to read differently later.
  4. If the shop writes the level on a form, take a photo of the form as well.

Reading a Rental Bike Fuel Gauge: Plan Range Without Guessing explains why a gauge reading is an estimate and how to read it. If the shop and you both note the odometer, Motorbike Trip Meter Versus Odometer: Record the Right Number shows which number to write.

When the gauge and the rule disagree

Gauges on small bikes are rough instruments. A needle that sits just above the last mark can mean very different amounts of fuel, and a bike that has been standing on its side stand may read differently from one that has been standing upright. That is why a rule of "the same level as at pickup" is only as exact as the two photos behind it, and why a rule of "full" is simpler to check: the pump stops, and everyone can see it stopped. If you and the shop read the same needle two ways, do not settle it by argument. Compare the two photos, agree whether the difference is worth a charge, and ask for the decision to be written on the receipt or in a short message.

Two situations deserve a question at pickup, not at return. If the bike is handed over with less fuel than the rule assumes (for example a part-empty tank under a "return it full" rule), ask the shop to note the level in writing before you ride away. If you expect to cover a long distance, ask whether the rule changes with the distance, since a rule written for a morning in town may not suit a day trip; Rental Motorbike Mileage Limits: Read the Odometer Clause Before a Long Trip covers the distance side.

Plan the refuel

If the rule is "same level" or "full", the fuel stop is part of the return, and it takes time. The shop is open 09:00–21:00 daily, so a return planned for 20:30 leaves very little room to find a pump, queue and still reach the counter. Decide where you will refuel the day before, and ask the shop whether a particular fuel type or grade is expected. If you have never refuelled a scooter, Refuelling a Rental Motorbike in Hanoi: A Photo Guide to the Pump and Scooter Fuel Cap and Seat Release: Learn the Correct Sequence at Handover show the sequence.

At the pump, switch the engine off, keep cigarettes and flames away, and stop when the pump stops rather than squeezing in more. If you ever smell petrol while the bike is parked, do not start it, keep flames and cigarettes away, move back and ask for help; see Motorbike Smells of Petrol While Parked: Stop, Move Away and Seek Help.

At the counter

Show your starting photo next to the gauge as it is now. If the two readings agree, the conversation is short. If they differ, say so and agree what the rule means before anyone talks about money. A reading near a boundary, for example a needle sitting between two marks, is a matter of judgment, so it helps to have the earlier photo and the shop's statement of the rule. Once the return is done, ask for a receipt or a short note that carries the real time; Returning a Rental Motorbike in Hanoi: A Receipt and Handover Checklist lists the other things a return record should hold.

To ask about the rule before you book, call 0334 699 969 or visit Ngõ 5 Nguyễn Văn Cừ, Bồ Đề, Long Biên, Hà Nội (near Gia Lâm bus station). The shop's delivery and pickup guide is the shop's pickup guide; it does not replace asking about the fuel rule.
